editorial:
Imagine waking up every single day and doing the exact same thing over and over. You follow a strict schedule, go to work, and come home to a quiet apartment. That is exactly how the main guy in this story lives his life. Everything is fine until he starts having weird problems with his building's elevator. What starts as a small annoyance quickly turns into a total nightmare. You can really feel the stress building up as he realizes he is not in control of his own home anymore. It feels like a bad dream that you just cannot wake up from, and it keeps you wondering if the machine is actually acting on its own.

The acting is great because you really feel for the guy as he loses his mind. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you like constant action. However, the tension makes up for it. If you enjoy stories about people fighting against things they cannot see or control, you will love this. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a big movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a smart move.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out the elevator was not just broken; it was actually targeting him. He tries to escape the building, but the elevator traps him one last time. The big twist is that he never actually leaves the lift. He ends up stuck in a loop of his own routine, forever trapped inside the machine. It wraps up with a dark feeling, showing that the machine finally won.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and early Robert Zemeckis work.
